title: Spring Lecture #23: Spring AOP Advice Types Explained

questions.question: You need to remove a `ThreadLocal` value after a service method finishes, whether it returned normally or threw an exception, and you don't need the result or the exception. Which advice fits most precisely?
options: `@AfterReturning`, because it runs after the method completes
`@After`, because it behaves like a `finally` block and runs on both success and failure
`@AfterThrowing`, because cleanup is mainly needed when something goes wrong
`@Before`, because the value must be cleared before the next call starts
questions.explanation: `@After` is 'after-finally' advice: it runs for every outcome and is the narrowest choice for outcome-neutral cleanup. `@AfterReturning` runs only on normal return, so the ThreadLocal would leak whenever the method throws. `@AfterThrowing` covers only the failure path.

questions.question: In a Spring Boot 4 project with `spring-boot-starter-aspectj`, you write the class below inside a subpackage of the main application package. The advice never prints anything when `createStudent()` is called. What is wrong?
options: `@Before` advice must take a `JoinPoint` parameter, otherwise it is skipped
The pointcut must use `within(...)` instead of `execution(...)` for service classes
`@EnableAspectJAutoProxy` must be added manually in every Spring Boot application
`@Aspect` only describes the class's role; without `@Component` (or a `@Bean`) it is never registered as a bean, so Spring never applies it
questions.explanation: `@Aspect` marks the class as containing pointcuts and advice, but it is not a stereotype, so component scanning does not register it. Adding `@Component` (as in the lecture's `LoggingAspect`) fixes it. The `JoinPoint` parameter is optional, and Spring Boot auto-configures the AOP proxy infrastructure when the starter is present.

questions.question: The controller calls `studentService.dummyMethod("aditya")` through the Spring proxy. What does the console show, and what does the controller receive?
options: "dummyMethod called", "Intercepted, calling again", "dummyMethod called"; the controller receives "aditya"
"dummyMethod called", "Intercepted, calling again"; the second `proceed()` is ignored and the controller receives "aditya"
"Intercepted, calling again", "dummyMethod called"; the controller receives "aditya"
"dummyMethod called" once, then an `IllegalStateException` because `proceed()` was already used
questions.explanation: `@Around` advice may call `proceed()` zero, one or several times, and each call runs the rest of the chain and the target again. So the target prints twice, with the advice's message between the two calls, and the advice returns the second result. This is why retrying with multiple `proceed()` calls is dangerous for side-effecting methods.

questions.question: The controller calls `studentService.dummyMethod("aditya")` and returns the result as the response body. What is printed, and what is the response body?
options: Prints "dummyMethod called: aditya"; body "aditya", because the original arguments are always passed to the target
Prints the original lowercase name (the target still sees the old arguments); body is the uppercase name followed by " : String Intercepted"
Prints "dummyMethod called: ADITYA"; body "ADITYA : String Intercepted"
Prints "dummyMethod called: ADITYA"; body "ADITYA", because `@Around` cannot change the return value
questions.explanation: `proceed(Object[])` invokes the target with the replacement arguments, so the method receives and prints "ADITYA". The value the around advice returns is what the caller sees, so the appended suffix reaches the controller. Changing both arguments and the result is exactly what only `@Around` can do.

questions.question: `makePayment()` contains `try { throw new RuntimeException("Gateway failed"); } catch (RuntimeException e) { return "Fallback response"; }`. An aspect has both `@AfterReturning` and `@AfterThrowing` advice on this method. Which advice runs?
options: Only `@AfterThrowing`, because an exception was thrown during the method
Only `@AfterReturning`, because the exception never escaped and the method exited normally
Both, because one exception was thrown and a value was returned
Neither, because a caught exception cancels all after-advice for that call
questions.explanation: Advice reacts to how the target method EXITS, not to events inside it. The exception was caught internally, and the method returned "Fallback response" normally, so `@AfterReturning` runs and `@AfterThrowing` does not. Thinking that `@AfterThrowing` fires for any thrown exception is the common misconception.

questions.question: A feature flag must stop `makePayment()` and return the string "Payments disabled" to the caller (no exception). Why can't a `@Before` advice do this, and what should be used?
options: `@Before` can do it by calling `joinPoint.skip()` and returning the string
`@Before` can do it if the advice method's return type is `String`; its return value replaces the result
`@Before` cannot access the method arguments, so it cannot check the flag; use `@AfterReturning` instead
`@Before` receives only a `JoinPoint`, which can inspect but not control the invocation, so it can only stop the call by throwing; use `@Around` and return the value without calling `proceed()`
questions.explanation: `JoinPoint` exposes the signature, arguments, target and proxy but has no way to skip the call or supply a result. A `@Before` advice can only prevent the target by throwing an exception. `@Around` with `ProceedingJoinPoint` can decide not to call `proceed()` and return an alternative value. A `@Before` advice's return value is simply ignored.

questions.question: All four advice methods are in the SAME aspect and match `createStudent()`, which prints "Student saved" and returns normally. In what order are the lines printed?
options: Before, Around-before, Student saved, Around-after, After, AfterReturning
Around-before, Before, Student saved, After, AfterReturning, Around-after
Around-before, Before, Student saved, AfterReturning, After, Around-after
Before, Around-before, Student saved, AfterReturning, Around-after, After
questions.explanation: Within one aspect, `@Around` has the highest precedence, so its pre-`proceed()` code runs first, followed by `@Before`, then the target. Following AspectJ's after-finally semantics, `@After` is effectively invoked after `@AfterReturning`. Only then does control return to the around advice for "Around-after". This matches the notes' final invocation-flow diagram.

questions.question: `placeOrder()` throws `new IllegalStateException("Out of stock")`. The caller wraps the call in `try { orderService.placeOrder(); } catch (RuntimeException e) { System.out.println("Caller caught: " + e.getMessage()); }`. What is printed?
options:
Clearing context
Caller caught: Out of stock

Invalid: Out of stock
Clearing context
Caller caught: Out of stock

Invalid: Out of stock
Clearing context
Clearing context
questions.explanation: The `throwing` parameter type restricts matching: this advice runs only for `IllegalArgumentException` (and subclasses), and `IllegalStateException` is not one. `@After` runs on every outcome, so "Clearing context" is printed. After-advice never swallows the exception, so it still reaches the caller's catch block.

questions.question: The lecture's `@AfterReturning(returning = "result")` advice on `createStudent(..)` takes a `Student result` and calls `result.setName("Rohit"); result.setAge(21);`. A client POSTs `{"name":"Aditya","age":25}`, and `createStudent()` returns the same `Student` object that the controller puts in `ResponseEntity.ok(...)`. What does the client receive?
options: `{"name":"Aditya","age":25}`, because `@AfterReturning` can never affect what the caller gets
A 500 error, because `@AfterReturning` advice is not allowed to call setters on the returned value
`{"name":"Aditya","age":25}`, because the advice receives a defensive copy of the returned object
`{"name":"Rohit","age":21}`, because the advice gets the same object reference and mutates it, even though it cannot return a different object
questions.explanation: `@AfterReturning` cannot replace the returned reference (any value the advice returns is ignored), but it receives the SAME object, so mutating it changes what the caller sees. The notes call this poor design because it hides data transformation outside the visible business flow. Use `@Around` for deliberate result changes, and keep `@AfterReturning` for observation.

questions.question: A timing aspect declares `@Around("execution(* com.app.service.*.*(..))") public void time(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp) throws Throwable { long t = System.nanoTime(); pjp.proceed(); System.out.println(System.nanoTime() - t); }`. After deploying it, `studentService.getStudent()` (returns `String`) suddenly returns `null` to the controller. Why?
options: `System.nanoTime()` cannot be used inside advice, which makes the proxy fall back to returning `null`
The around advice is `void`, so the value from `proceed()` is discarded and the caller always gets `null`; it should return `Object` and return the `proceed()` result
`proceed()` must be called with `pjp.getArgs()` explicitly, otherwise the target receives no arguments and returns `null`
Around advice always returns `null` for `String` methods unless `returning = "result"` is configured
questions.explanation: What the around advice returns is what the caller observes. A `void` around advice discards the `proceed()` result, so the caller always gets `null`. A generic around advice should be declared `Object` and return the result (ideally with the timing in a `finally` block so failures are timed too). `proceed()` with no arguments reuses the original arguments, and `returning` is an `@AfterReturning` attribute.
